title: Interaction induced flattening of optical transition quantum geometry
authors: Xu Yang, Justin C. W. Song
abstract: The Riemannian geometry of optical transition dipoles has become a useful picture for understanding linear and nonlinear optical response. Here we argue that the interacting quantum geometry of optical transitions possesses a rich structure and can be naturally delineated into two types: localized and delocalized particle-hole excitations. The former possess uniform quantum geometry with flat (vanishing) Hermitian curvature; the latter possess non-uniform quantum geometry with non-vanishing Hermitian curvature. As a striking example, we find that uniform quantum geometry can be produced by electron-hole interactions: even when composed from extended Bloch states in the particle and hole bands, we find excitons have uniform and flat quantum geometry. By developing a many-body length gauge formulation of nonlinear response, we find this uniform and flat excitonic quantum geometry zeros its third-order circular photoconductivity in non-magnetic materials in stark contrast to its non-interacting counterparts. Similarly, the zero Hermitian curvature of localized optical transitions locks their Hall response to that of the ground state. This demonstrates the rich landscape of many-body optical response controlled by an interacting quantum geometry.
summary: This work develops a geometric framework to describe optical transitions in interacting quantum materials, classifying excitations into localized (flat geometry) and delocalized (curved geometry) types. The key finding is that the flat geometry of excitons forces the third-order photoconductivity to zero, offering a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding many-body optical response.
main_problem: The paper investigates how electron-electron interactions modify the resonant quantum geometry of optical transitions and establishes a link between this geometry and nonlinear optical response.
main_result: Interactions induce a rich structure in the quantum geometry, leading to localized excitations (excitons) possessing a uniform and flat geometry ($K=0$), which causes the third-order circular photoconductivity to vanish.
method: The analysis employs a many-body length gauge formulation to characterize the geometry using Hermitian metrics, connections, and curvature tensors, contrasting localized and delocalized excitation regimes.
model_or_system: The study models optical transitions in interacting many-body electronic materials, using concepts like particle-hole excitations and relative coordinate localization to parameterize the quantum geometry.
key_observables: Hermitian curvature tensor ($K$), third-order circular photoconductivity, and the Berry curvature ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: The distinction between localized (excitonic) and delocalized excitations; the limit of vanishing frequency ($\omega_\Sigma 	o 0$).
main_assumptions: The formulation relies on extending the length-gauge framework to interacting many-body systems, and localized excitations are assumed to exhibit relative coordinate localization.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the difference between non-flat and interaction-induced flat resonant quantum geometry via parallel transport, and shows calculated Hermitian curvature tensors for delocalized versus excitonic transitions in MoS2.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the geometry formulation, analyzes the constraints imposed by flux threading, derives expressions for nonlinear currents (injection and shift), and finally applies these results to specific material examples like MoS2.
why_interesting: The explicit connection drawn between geometric properties (flatness/curvature) and measurable nonlinear optical responses (photoconductivity) provides a powerful, unifying theoretical framework for understanding many-body optical phenomena.
